profile.summary: LncRFM is an RNA foundation model built for long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs), whose function depends on both short sequence motifs and base pairing that can span thousands of nucleotides. It reads an RNA sequence and is pretrained to predict masked nucleotides, with masking guided by secondary structure; its encoder outputs can then be fine-tuned with a small task head for tasks such as lncRNA localisation, disease association or splice-site prediction. The authors also release the LncCorpus pretraining corpus and the LncBench benchmark.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: LncRFM is a hybrid bidirectional state-space encoder: a convolutional motif stem with kernel widths 3 and 7, then 12 blocks of which ten are non-causal bidirectional selective state-space mixers and two are self-attention blocks with 12 heads, at embedding dimension 768. Pretraining is masked RNA modelling from random initialisation: 15% of non-special tokens are selected, of which 80% are replaced by [MASK], 10% by a random nucleotide and 10% left unchanged, and nucleotide reconstruction is the only objective. Predicted base pairing enters in two ways. A binary pairing indicator feeds a learnable gate that mixes the forward and reverse state-space scans. And after a warm-in phase of about 42% of the run, batches are increasingly chosen for joint masking, in which the predicted partner of a selected paired nucleotide is masked at the same time, reaching about 14.8% of batches at the end of the run and about 4% averaged over it. Downstream inference uses primary sequence alone, with the two directions simply averaged.

sections.title: Training setup
sections.body: The paper reports pretraining on four data-parallel GPU processes in FP32, with a per-process microbatch of 20 and gradient accumulation of 2, so an effective batch of 160 sequences per update, over 300,000 updates. The optimiser was AdamW at a peak learning rate of 2e-4, beta1 0.9, beta2 0.999, no weight decay, 1,000 warm-up updates then linear decay, with gradients clipped at 0.5 and batches grouped by length. The GPU model and the wall-clock cost are not stated. Downstream work froze the encoder and trained only a bottleneck adapter and head, and the software stack was Python 3.9.23, PyTorch 2.3.1 and Transformers 4.44.0.

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: Hybrid bidirectional state-space encoder. The paper describes a multiscale convolutional motif stem with depthwise-separable branches of kernel widths 3 and 7, then 12 residual blocks: ten non-causal bidirectional selective state-space mixers (state dimension 64, local convolution width 7, expansion factor 2, head dimension 64) and two multi-head self-attention blocks with 12 heads of dimension 64. Embedding dimension 768, and no learned absolute positional embeddings. During pretraining a learnable scalar gate per block mixes the forward and reverse states according to whether a nucleotide has a predicted pairing partner; at adaptation and inference the two directions are averaged instead, from sequence alone. The paper puts the attention blocks at 6 and 12 while model_config.json lists attention layers 5 and 11, so the two sources differ.

facts.label: Training data
facts.value: LncCorpus: 24,771,981 RNA sequence and structure records (sequence plus pairing partners) in 86 Parquet files. The paper says it combined RNAcentral transcripts with pairing indices from the MUSES ensemble for sequences up to 512 nt and from LinearFold for longer ones, added over 9.6 million long non-coding and transcript sequences of its own to a source corpus of 31,121,367 records, and filtered that to sequences of 200 to 2,050 nt with matching sequence and pairing-vector lengths, leaving 24,648,121 pretraining sequences and 123,860 held-out validation sequences. Pretraining ran about two epochs over that corpus in 300,000 updates. CC BY 4.0 for the project's own contributions; upstream data keep their terms.

steps.title: Predict a masked nucleotide
steps.shell:
python - <<'EOF'
from pathlib import Path
import json
import torch
from lncrfm import get_lncrfm, get_tokenizer

checkpoint = Path("checkpoints/lncrfm_pretrained")
options = json.loads((checkpoint / "model_config.json").read_text())["factory_kwargs"]
tokenizer = get_tokenizer(
    tokenizer_file=str(checkpoint / "tokenizer.json"),
    max_length=options["max_length"],
)
model = get_lncrfm(
    **options,
    tokenizer=tokenizer,
    from_pretrained=str(checkpoint),
    dtype=torch.float32,
    device="cuda",
).eval()

inputs = tokenizer("[CLS] A U G [MASK] C [SEP]", return_tensors="pt").to("cuda")
with torch.no_grad():
    outputs = model(**inputs)
print(outputs.logits.argmax(dim=-1))
EOF

notes: The README's install commands assume a cloned repository; the clone and download lines in the run guide were added from the repository URL, the Zenodo file link and the archive's file list. Three small members of the weights archive (model_config.json, README.md, LICENSE) and its central directory were read with HTTP range requests rather than downloading the 178 MB file; the saved member files are the inflated contents. The full text of the preprint is now saved and quoted from its pdftotext layer; the bioRxiv banner gives its licence as CC-BY-NC 4.0, so store_bytes is false, and the Europe PMC abstract is kept as a source. No IP-address stamp was found in the text layer. Two sources disagree about where the self-attention blocks sit: the paper says blocks 6 and 12, model_config.json lists attention layers 5 and 11; the page states both. The paper's corpus filtering range (200 to 2,050 nt) also differs from the maximum length in pretrain.sh (2,048). The earlier note that GitHub reports the repository licence as NOASSERTION is removed, because no saved source for this model records a GitHub API response; the LICENSE file is MIT with an added upstream notice.
